Hannah / Marissa —

Proposed credit structure (keeping ops and precedent in mind):
- Offer: 500,000 token evaluation credit (equivalent to our standard 30-day eval)
- Extension: one-time 7-day extension upon request (no additional credit), requires a short justification email from the customer and approval from Sales Ops
- Guardrails: limit to hosted Redwood models (no private on-prem variants), max concurrency 8 requests/s, no model fine-tuning or dataset uploads that would retain customer data beyond caching TTL (we can allow ephemeral KV use)
- Attribution: credit is tied to account DF-2026-RFP-78, single-use only, cannot be transferred to other orgs

Attachments: credit-structure-matrix.xlsx (breaks down token equivalence vs. our pricing tiers), procurement-terms-draft.docx (simple note procurement can sign).

Rationale: 500k tokens is large enough to run their 10k-conversation load for generation-lite tests but small enough that we limit downstream infra cost. If this moves to Dedicated later, we can treat credits as a discount on first-month committed spend.

Approval path: sales manager sign-off + Sales Ops record. For exceptional ask (larger credit or extended extension) escalate to Revenue Ops.

If you want, I can author a short confirmation note for procurement that includes the above guardrails and a DocuSign link.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
